triage_candidates.statement: gate_spec.evaluate_axis/evaluate_gate has no minimum-car-season-coverage floor at the AXIS level: an axis-beat is counted as a binary pass regardless of how many car-seasons contributed (n_car_seasons_considered is reported but NOT gated on). Demonstrated concretely: the g1 test suite's own F1/F3 tests (test_genuine_improver_passes_guard_and_registers_beat, test_seven_of_eleven_beats_passes_the_gate) already exercise exactly n=1 covered car-season (CS_DEV only; CS_B/CS_C never get model_col) per toy axis, and that registers as a full 'beat' toward the >=7/11 tally. This means a real g2-g5 model that legitimately abstains/floats on hard car-seasons (DC1's own sanctioned honest-null pattern for Layer 2) could win an axis-beat by covering only its easiest 1-2 car-seasons, without any coverage-fraction penalty in the binary n_beats>=7 rule. Not in scope of F1/F2/F3 as literally frozen by the launch order (over-shrinkage, pairing, bootstrap-unit -- all correctly implemented), and NOT something g1's implementer had authority to unilaterally add (Authority section: 'implement it exactly; do not soften or re-tune'). Recommend Commander/Admiral decide before g5 whether evaluate_gate needs a per-axis minimum-coverage floor (e.g. n_car_seasons_considered >= some fraction of total held-out car-seasons) before an axis-beat counts, or whether this is an accepted risk given the MDE/power sanity helper already exists as a softer signal.
